enonce.texte: Objectif : Identifier et définir des concepts abstraits en anglais.

questions.texte: Associez chaque concept abstrait à sa définition.

sousQuestions.texte: Happiness
sousQuestions.reponse: Happiness is the state of being happy, feeling joy, contentment, or satisfaction.

sousQuestions.texte: Success
sousQuestions.reponse: Success is the accomplishment of a goal or purpose. It is the achievement of something desired.

sousQuestions.texte: Freedom
sousQuestions.reponse: Freedom is the power or right to act, speak, or think without hindrance or restraint.

sousQuestions.texte: Justice
sousQuestions.reponse: Justice is the quality of being fair, just, and morally right. It involves treating people equitably.

enonce.texte: Objectif : Utiliser des structures avancées pour exprimer des opinions nuancées.

questions.texte: Complétez les phrases suivantes avec l'expression appropriée pour exprimer une opinion nuancée. Utilisez les mots : tend to, it seems to me that, I would argue that, from my perspective, it could be argued that.

sousQuestions.texte: ______ success is not only about money but also about personal fulfillment.
sousQuestions.reponse: I would argue that success is not only about money but also about personal fulfillment.

sousQuestions.texte: ______ happiness is more important than wealth.
sousQuestions.reponse: From my perspective, happiness is more important than wealth.

sousQuestions.texte: People ______ equate freedom with the ability to do whatever they want.
sousQuestions.reponse: People tend to equate freedom with the ability to do whatever they want.

sousQuestions.texte: ______ that justice is not always served in our society.
sousQuestions.reponse: It could be argued that justice is not always served in our society.

sousQuestions.texte: ______ that happiness is a choice rather than a result of circumstances.
sousQuestions.reponse: It seems to me that happiness is a choice rather than a result of circumstances.

enonce.texte: Objectif : Participer à une discussion de groupe sur des sujets abstraits en utilisant des structures avancées et un vocabulaire varié.

questions.texte: En petits groupes (3-4 personnes), discutez du sujet suivant : 'What is the meaning of success?' Utilisez les expressions de la leçon et des exemples concrets.
questions.reponse: Réponse libre. Exemple de contribution : 'I would argue that success is personal and subjective. From my perspective, success is achieving your personal goals, whatever they may be. For some, it's financial independence; for others, it's having a happy family. It seems to me that society often imposes a narrow definition of success.'

sousQuestions.texte: Chaque participant doit exprimer son opinion sur le sujet en utilisant au moins 2 expressions nuancées.
Le groupe doit ensuite discuter des différences et des points communs entre les opinions exprimées.

enonce.texte: Objectif : Mener une discussion philosophique sur un sujet abstrait en utilisant un langage nuancé.

questions.texte: Lisez la citation suivante : 'Freedom is the right to do what you want, as long as it does not harm others. Justice is the principle that everyone should be treated fairly.' Discutez de la relation entre la liberté et la justice.
questions.reponse: Réponse libre. Exemple : 'It could be argued that freedom and justice are closely linked. From my perspective, true freedom cannot exist without justice because unfair treatment limits people's opportunities. However, I would argue that too much freedom can lead to injustice if individuals abuse their rights. It seems to me that societies must find a balance between these two principles.'

sousQuestions.texte: La liberté peut-elle exister sans justice ?
La justice limite-t-elle la liberté ?
Quel est le rôle du gouvernement dans l'équilibre entre liberté et justice ?

enonce.texte: Objectif : Rédiger une réflexion personnelle sur un concept abstrait en utilisant des structures avancées.

questions.texte: Rédigez un essai de 250 mots sur le sujet : 'What does happiness mean to you?' Structurez votre texte avec une introduction, un développement et une conclusion. Utilisez au moins 5 expressions pour exprimer des opinions nuancées.
questions.reponse: Réponse libre. Exemple : 'Introduction: Happiness is a universal human desire, but its definition varies greatly from person to person. From my perspective, happiness is not about material possessions but about meaningful connections and personal growth. Body: It seems to me that society often confuses happiness with pleasure. I would argue that true happiness comes from pursuing meaningful goals and building strong relationships. For example, helping others and spending time with loved ones bring me more joy than buying new things. Conclusion: In conclusion, happiness is a deeply personal concept. I tend to believe that it is found in the small moments of life and in the relationships we build.'

sousQuestions.texte: Introduction : présentez votre thèse sur le bonheur.
Développement : développez 2-3 arguments avec des exemples concrets.
Conclusion : résumez votre position et ouvrez sur une réflexion.

enonce.texte: Objectif : Participer à un débat structuré sur un sujet abstrait en utilisant des arguments nuancés.

questions.texte: Organisez un débat en binôme ou en groupe sur la question : 'Is freedom an illusion?'
questions.reponse: Réponse libre. Exemple d'arguments : Pour (le libre arbitre existe) : 'I would argue that freedom is real. We make choices every day, and these choices shape our lives. It seems to me that we are responsible for our actions.' Contre (le libre arbitre est une illusion) : 'It could be argued that our choices are influenced by factors beyond our control, such as our upbringing and social environment. From my perspective, true freedom is limited.'

sousQuestions.texte: Préparez 3 arguments en faveur de la position.
Préparez 3 arguments contre la position.
Répondez aux arguments de l'autre camp en utilisant des expressions nuancées.
